rows.claim: The validated pipeline genuinely detects true criticality: on a critical (m=1.0) Galton-Watson positive control it calls 'critical' at a high rate.
rows.evidence: 2026-06-11_cc_data.json scan[n=300].crit_TPR = 0.817 (Wilson 95% CI [0.738, 0.876]); TPR stays 0.93-0.98 across n=500..2500
rows.scope: synthetic Galton-Watson critical branching process (Poisson offspring m=1.0); single fixed pipeline (discrete Hurwitz-zeta MLE, KS-minimised x_min, asymptotic KS threshold, crackling band 20%, n_aval>=150 gate)

rows.claim: At literature-typical sample sizes the same pipeline is a diagnostic detector of criticality, i.e. it does NOT raise false positives on matched non-critical controls (registered falsifier: FPR < 0.20).
rows.evidence: 2026-06-11_cc_data.json matched subcritical m=0.9: scan[n=300].subcrit_FPR = 0.408 [0.325, 0.498]; n=500 = 0.467 [0.380, 0.556]; n=800 = 0.392 [0.309, 0.481] — lower CI bound at every n is well above the 0.20 rejection threshold
rows.scope: matched subcritical Galton-Watson control (m=0.9) at n_aval = 300/500/800, the literature-typical regime; passes power-law AND crackling tests at these false-positive rates

rows.claim: The diagnosticity claimed for the pipeline is a property of the pipeline, holding at the sample sizes real avalanche experiments use.
rows.evidence: FPR only falls below the 0.05 diagnostic target outside the literature-typical regime: scan[n=1500].subcrit_FPR = 0.100 [0.06,0.17]; scan[n=2500] = 0.042 [0.018, 0.094]; n=4000 = 0.008
rows.scope: sample-size scan 300..4000; the sub-0.05 regime begins only at n_aval >= 2500, an order of magnitude above typical avalanche counts

rows.claim: At the single intermediate size n=1500 the registered falsifier did not literally fire (FPR < 0.20), the point on which the thesis side was briefly correct.
rows.evidence: scan[n=1500].subcrit_FPR = 0.100 [0.06, 0.17]; point estimate and upper CI both below the 0.20 trigger — the counter-side had read the CI upper bound as the estimate
rows.scope: one intermediate sample size only; does not rescue the registered thesis, which is stated for literature-typical n where FPR is 0.39-0.47

rows.claim: The counter-side's exotic surrogates (AR(1), shot-noise) are what defeat the pipeline.
rows.evidence: not reproduced — the counter-side's AR(1) and shot-noise counterexamples failed to replicate on rerun; the decisive evidence is the thesis side's OWN matched-subcritical FPR table, not these surrogates
rows.scope: transcript surrogates outside the decisive repro; quarantined as non-reproducing

rows.claim: Real cortical dynamics are (or are not) critical; real avalanche data are misdiagnosed by this pipeline.
rows.evidence: not tested — synthetic Galton-Watson branching process only; no real neural recordings, no real detection/binning pipeline, no empirical control
rows.scope: would require running the pipeline on real cortical avalanche recordings with matched empirical controls; not run

rows.claim: The positive-control true-positive rate is itself stable across all sample sizes.
rows.evidence: scan[n=4000].crit_TPR = 0.900 [0.833, 0.942]: TPR begins to erode at large n because the KS-minimised x_min trims short avalanches intrinsic to the critical distribution — a separate finite-size/estimator tension
rows.scope: large-n positive control only; not part of the headline FPR claim
